ordered_diagnoses: Multisystem proteinopathy due to TBK1 mutations

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological decline with bulbar and cognitive involvement
salient_findings: Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia
key_facts: 6-month history of progressive symptoms
Family history of memory problems after age 80
Cognitive impairment on neurological examination
Vertical gaze palsy on neurological examination
Tongue atrophy on neurological examination
Pyramidal signs on neurological examination
Severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia on 11C-CFT PET imaging
Almost total loss of dopamine transporter binding in caudate nucleus
Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene identified by whole-exon sequencing
Autoimmune encephalitis antibodies negative in serum and CSF
Large-amplitude, long-duration motor unit potential on needle EMG of frontalis, mentalis, orbicularis oculi, and genioglossus muscles

shortlist.label: Multisystem proteinopathy due to TBK1 mutations
shortlist.why_kept: Heterozygous pathogenic variant of TBK1 gene and multisystem involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of a heterozygous pathogenic variant of the TBK1 gene, along with symptoms such as progressive dysarthria, dysphagia, cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, tongue atrophy, and pyramidal signs, supports this diagnosis. The severe loss of dopamine transporter binding in basal ganglia and almost total loss in the caudate nucleus on 11C-CFT PET imaging also aligns with this condition.

rejected.label: Frontotemporal dementia
rejected.why: While frontotemporal dementia could explain some cognitive and motor symptoms, the specific genetic finding of a TBK1 mutation and the pattern of dopamine transporter loss point more specifically to TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
rejected.why: Although ALS could explain some motor symptoms like tongue atrophy and pyramidal signs, it does not account for the cognitive impairment, vertical gaze palsy, or the specific pattern of dopamine transporter loss seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Progressive supranuclear palsy
rejected.why: While progressive supranuclear palsy could explain vertical gaze palsy and some parkinsonian features, the genetic findings and the specific pattern of dopamine transporter loss are more consistent with TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia.

rejected.label: Multisystem proteinopathy due to TBK1 mutations
rejected.why: This diagnosis is considered because of the TBK1 mutation, but the clinical presentation and imaging findings more specifically support TBK1-associated frontotemporal dementia as the primary diagnosis, given the emphasis on dementia and specific neuroimaging results.
